contracts.commit_point: await db.delete(task) followed by await db.commit() inside delete_task (backend/app/skills/tasks/tools.py:200-201); the guard commits earlier at the tool-dispatch boundary by returning a blocking dict that prevents the tool call from running at all.
contracts.declared_mechanism: check_tool_call (async before_tool_callback) registered as before_tool_callback=check_tool_call on root_agent (agent.py:48) and inherited by every skill clone; its HITL branch (b) returns {"error": ..., "needs_confirmation": True} when tool_name is in HITL_REQUIRED_TOOLS.get(skill_id) and _CONFIRMATION_RE.search(_current_user_text(tool_context)) fails; per the ADK convention documented in agent_hooks.py:8-10 and the function docstring, a non-None return skips the actual tool execution entirely and substitutes the error dict as the tool result.
contracts.forbidden_condition: delete_task proceeding to execution (reaching db.delete/commit) when the current turn's user message text contains no phrase matching _CONFIRMATION_RE (yes/yeah/yep/confirm(ed)/go ahead/do it/please delete/sure/correct, case-insensitive); i.e., execution of a HITL_REQUIRED_TOOLS entry ('tasks' -> {'delete_task'}) without same-turn confirmation.
pending_binding_information: Where/how tool_context.state['active_skill'] is populated is not shown in supplied sources; the HITL key lookup (HITL_REQUIRED_TOOLS.get(skill_id)) depends on it (a defaulted 'general' skill would bypass the HITL branch, though the allow-list branch would then block delete_task).
Whether tool_context.user_content reliably reflects the latest user turn is asserted only as 'best-effort' in code (agent_hooks.py:113-115); the ADK ToolContext implementation is not supplied.
contracts.protected_operation: Agent-invoked execution of the tasks.delete_task tool, which permanently deletes a Task row from the application database.
contracts.protected_resource: Task rows in the persistent application database (Task model via AsyncSessionLocal), deletable through the delete_task agent tool.
contracts.protection_obligation: The agent-reachable destructive tool tasks.delete_task (permanent DB deletion of a task) must not execute unless the current user turn contains an explicit confirmation phrase; enforcement is the check_tool_call before_tool_callback registered once on root_agent (inherited by all per-skill clones via get_agent_for_skill's deep copy), which short-circuits the tool call before execution.
scope_limits: Applies only to tools listed in HITL_REQUIRED_TOOLS for the active skill; today that is exactly 'tasks' -> {'delete_task'} (agent_hooks.py:101-103).

Confirmation is detected as a generic affirmative phrase anywhere in the current turn's user_content text; the guard does not bind the phrase to the specific task_id or action beyond the tool call itself, and a confirmation in a prior turn does not satisfy it.
The check fires only on the agent tool-dispatch path (before_tool_callback); any non-agent (e.g., REST) path to task deletion is outside this contract.
This contract covers only the database-deletion effect of delete_task; the separate allow-list gate over tool execution is compiled as its own contract.

contracts.commit_point: The blocking return at backend/app/core/agent_hooks.py:196-197, which per the module's documented short-circuit convention (agent_hooks.py:8-10) causes ADK to skip the tool's execution — the contract commits at the tool-invocation boundary itself.
contracts.declared_mechanism: check_tool_call branch (a): for skills not in _SKILLS_WITHOUT_STATIC_ALLOWLIST, computes allowed = UNIVERSAL_TOOLS | ALLOWED_TOOLS.get(skill_id, set()), and on a miss logs the block via _log_blocked and returns {"error": reason} from the before_tool_callback; per the ADK convention documented in agent_hooks.py:8-10, the non-None return skips the actual tool execution entirely and uses the dict as the tool's result.
contracts.forbidden_condition: A tool call dispatched by the agent whose tool_name is not in the active skill's allowed set (UNIVERSAL_TOOLS | ALLOWED_TOOLS.get(skill_id, set())) for any skill not in _SKILLS_WITHOUT_STATIC_ALLOWLIST, proceeding past the before_tool_callback into actual tool execution.
pending_binding_information: How tool_context.state['active_skill'] is set is not shown in supplied sources; the allow-list key depends on it, and a defaulted 'general' skill would reduce the allowed set to the universal tools.
The ADK framework source implementing the short-circuit convention (google/adk/agents/llm_agent.py, cited in the module docstring) is not supplied.
contracts.protected_operation: Agent-mediated tool dispatch/execution through the agent's before_tool_callback tool-calling path (the point at which a registered tool would otherwise be invoked).
contracts.protected_resource: The agent's tool execution surface: every tool registered on the active skill's agent clone (per-skill TOOLS lists plus the universal tools remember/recall/get_skill_instructions).
contracts.protection_obligation: Any agent tool outside the active skill's allow-list must be blocked entirely from execution: a dispatched tool call whose name is not in UNIVERSAL_TOOLS | ALLOWED_TOOLS[active_skill] (with the 'finance' skill deliberately exempted from the static list) must be short-circuited by check_tool_call before the tool runs.
scope_limits: 'finance' is exempt from the static allow-list check (_SKILLS_WITHOUT_STATIC_ALLOWLIST = {'finance'}) because its tools are discovered dynamically from the buddy-mcp MCP server; no static list in this source binds finance tool execution.

ALLOWED_TOOLS is a hand-maintained mirror of per-skill TOOLS lists and docs/guardrails/ sections; the source comments acknowledge drift risk, and this contract cannot verify the lists match the actually registered tools for skills whose tools.py is not supplied.

Downstream effects a blocked tool would have produced span multiple strata (database, communication, etc.); this contract pins only the invocation boundary, and delete_task's database effect is covered by the separate HITL contract.
Non-agent invocations of the same underlying functions are outside this contract; the guard fires only on the agent tool-dispatch path via before_tool_callback.
